raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Problem

Long regular HF fast-tokenizer calls in `TokenizerManager._tokenize_texts()` block the asyncio event loop and delay handlers such as `/ping`. Moving the call to a worker is insufficient if loop-side callers still share its native backend: a padding/truncation update can wait on the worker's encode.

Addresses the regular HF fast-tokenizer case in #30770. OpenAI conversion is already offloaded by merged #39771; this PR leaves that implementation in place.

## Changes

- Give regular HF fast tokenization one worker and a separate native backend, cloned once at startup. Pass the tokenizer explicitly to the worker rather than swapping `self.tokenizer` or introducing context-dependent tokenizer properties.
- Shallow-copy the wrapper per call so later wrapper settings are reflected without copying the vocabulary on the request path. Propagate request contextvars.
- Preserve synchronous behavior for slow/custom tokenizers and a tokenizer whose backend has been replaced. Preserve the dynamic-batch branch, cross-encoder/result handling and existing OpenAI conversion parallelism.
- Add registered CPU coverage for loop and real ASGI `/generate` + `/ping` responsiveness, backend separation, current wrapper settings, fallback behavior, serialization and context propagation. HTTP tests substitute model execution.

The backend-isolation direction follows @chromecast56's work and @hnyls2002's [shared-tokenizer review on #39716](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39716#discussion_r4150104467). #39716 and @JianWang97's #44502 both build on this PR; [coordination to choose one merge path](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30771#issuecomment-6561204899) is open. This can remain a small prerequisite or be folded into #39716 with attribution preserved.

## Validation

Base: `e2982985110fb432fd8ddba5f0147a5004fd03ab`.

- **388 passed, 376 subtests passed** across the focused tests, request cleanup/configuration, chat, completions, embeddings, Responses, transcription and tokenize endpoints.
- Focused tests on the unmodified base: **2 expected starvation failures, 1 passed, 3 helper-specific skips**. The candidate passes all 6 focused tests.
- Applicable pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed.
- Synthetic CPU WordLevel contention probe, actual candidate `_tokenize_texts`, `tokenizers==0.23.2`: a loop-side padding call during a 250k-token encode waited **296–307 ms** with a deliberately shared-backend control, versus **0.20–0.33 ms** with the candidate's separate backend (3 trials each; matching token outputs).

Local checks used macOS arm64 / Python 3.11.13, Transformers 5.19.0 and the repository's CPU kernel-stubbing helper. The contention probe is a synthetic correctness investigation, not a GPU or model-serving benchmark. Short-prompt `bench_serving` TTFT at low/high concurrency remains unvalidated. Upstream lint [passed on `e0a728540`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41331126976). Upstream test execution remains blocked on the missing `run-ci` label ([current gate](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41331127133/job/124921265674)); maintainer review remains pending.

## Scope and limits

This adds one native-backend copy per tokenizer manager. Runtime vocabulary mutation is outside this change; backend replacements retain the synchronous path. Slow/custom tokenizer offload, other endpoint preprocessing and global ordering/admission behavior remain separate work. There is no model, kernel, or KV-cache change.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code and run applicable pre-commit checks.
- [x] Add registered CPU unit and HTTP regression coverage.
- [x] Preserve the existing dynamic tokenizer and OpenAI conversion paths.
- [x] No new user-facing configuration required.

@merrymercy @slin1237 This PR is ready for review. Could an authorized maintainer add the `run-ci` label and trigger the full CI (for example, `/tag-and-rerun-ci`)? I do not have CI-label permission.

Local validation: 142 related tests passed. The two focused responsiveness tests and the ASGI integration test fail with the expected starvation assertions on unmodified `main`; the ASGI test now queues real `/v1/chat/completions` and `/ping` requests before yielding to the event loop.

@JustinTong0323 @merrymercy Gentle ping when you have a chance. This PR is ready for review and touches the OpenAI request-preprocessing path and TokenizerManager ownership boundary. The related unit and ASGI regression tests pass locally; I would especially appreciate feedback on the offloading and serialization approach. Thank you!

Rebased this PR on the latest `main`; the previous merge conflict is resolved and the branch now includes the current `MIN_BASE_SHA` gate from #21065.

This is the one PR I would like to prioritize for review.

Impact:
- Synchronous OpenAI request conversion and regular tokenization can block the API/tokenizer event loop.
- That can delay lightweight liveness endpoints such as `/ping` and `/health` even while the backend is otherwise alive.
- The patch keeps the existing serialized preprocessing behavior, but runs the blocking work in a `TokenizerManager`-owned single-thread executor.

Local validation after rebase:
- `ruff check` on all changed files
- `py_compile` on all changed files
- `scripts/ci/check_registered_tests.py`
- `git diff --check`
- Focused CPU unit tests: `test_serving_base_event_loop.py` and `test_tokenizer_manager_event_loop.py` passed locally with a macOS-only `torch.compile` import stub used for collection.

The ASGI liveness test was not rerun successfully in my local macOS environment because collection now requires optional local dependencies such as `mlx`; it should be covered by CI.

Could an authorized maintainer trigger CI with `/tag-and-rerun-ci` and review the frontend offloading boundary? I would especially appreciate feedback from @JustinTong0323 on the OpenAI serving path, @slin1237 for Router/API ownership, and @merrymercy / @hnyls2002 for the TokenizerManager / manager boundary.

Hi @merrymercy @hnyls2002 — gentle ping on this one. Routing to you two as the most active recent committers on `tokenizer_manager.py` / `http_server.py` (apologies if someone else is a better fit).

Quick summary for triage:
- **Problem**: synchronous request preprocessing blocks the TokenizerManager event loop, so `/health` stalls while tokens are still generating → Kubernetes liveness kills otherwise-healthy pods. We hit this in production at Toss Securities (271 gateway 502s from liveness restarts under load).
- **Fix**: offload the blocking preprocessing to a single-thread executor — no behavior change otherwise.
- **Status**: branch is up to date with `main` (0 behind), 142 tests pass locally (137 existing + 5 new, including an ASGI reproducer). The remaining red checks are the `pr-test-*-finish` gates — the underlying test stages show as skipped, so I believe CI just needs a maintainer trigger.

Happy to adjust scope or approach if you'd prefer a different design. Thanks!

We are seeing the same false-health-check issue in production with DeepSeek-V4-Flash on SGLang v0.5.16: synchronous request preprocessing can starve `/health` while inference is still making progress.

We backported this PR onto our existing v0.5.16 image and ran the same 448-concurrent-client load test with ~64k-token chat inputs. Before the patch, the baseline produced 4 new readiness timeouts in the first minute. With this PR applied, the same load ran for 10+ minutes with zero readiness timeouts, zero liveness timeouts, and zero request errors.

Rebased onto current `main` and re-verified end to end. Putting the case for merging in one place, because I think this one has sat long enough.

## The bug still reproduces on today's `main`

I re-ran the reproducer from #30770 against current `main` with only the new tests applied and no production change: both starvation tests **fail**. With this PR applied they pass. So this is not a historical report — the synchronous preprocessing path is still on the event loop today, two months after the issue was filed.

Concretely, `OpenAIServingBase.handle_request()` calls `_convert_to_internal_request()` synchronously (Jinja render + `tokenizer.encode()`), and `TokenizerManager._tokenize_texts()` has a synchronous fallback. Both run on the same uvicorn loop as `/ping`, `/health` and `/health_generate`.

## Why the failure mode is worse than "a slow endpoint"

The engine is fine the whole time. Inference keeps making progress; only the loop cannot get a turn to answer the probe. So an orchestrator with a liveness probe restarts a **healthy** server, drops its in-flight requests, and pushes that load onto the remaining replicas — which then starve the same way. A transient burst becomes a rolling restart, and nothing in the logs points at preprocessing. That is why #30770 uses `/ping` rather than `/health`: it isolates loop responsiveness from generation health.

## Independent production confirmation

@yongqinwang-cmd hit this on a different model and a different deployment, backported the patch, and measured it (see above): 4 readiness timeouts in the first minute before, zero over 10+ minutes after, at 448 concurrent clients with ~64k-token inputs. They are carrying it as a local patch today.

## The change is small and deliberately conservative

`+412/-11` across 5 files, of which **378 lines are tests**. The production change is 29 added lines:

- A `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)` — *single* worker on purpose. Preprocessing is moved off the loop but stays serialized, so this cannot trade event-loop starvation for CPU oversubscription under a container quota.
- `copy_context().run(...)` so contextvars survive the thread hop.
- Both blocking paths routed through it.

## What I fixed in this push

Two things had rotted while the branch waited, both now handled:

- `_tokenize_texts` began consulting `model_config.is_embedding_gemma` after these tests were written, so the bare-manager test needed that attribute stubbed.
- The registered-test taxonomy (`test/registered/<kind>/<subsystem>/`) landed since the branch was opened, and the ASGI liveness test was outside it. Moved to `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/`; `check_registered_tests.py` and `check_no_registered_tests_in_package.py` now both pass.

Verified locally: the two CPU responsiveness tests pass with the patch and fail without it. The ASGI test could not run in my environment (`mlx` is not installable here), so I am relying on CI for that one.

## What is actually blocking this

Per [MAINTAINER.md](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md), this PR never got past step 2 — no Merge Oncall was ever assigned — so step 3 never happened either and it has **no `run-ci` label**. Every red check above is `pr-gate` refusing to start; not one test has ever run on this branch in CI. I am not in `.github/CI_PERMISSIONS.json`, so `/tag-and-rerun-ci` is a no-op for me.

Step 4 permits pinging other area oncalls when the assigned one is unresponsive. This touches `srt/entrypoints` and `srt/managers`:

- Router / API — @slin1237
- Scheduler — @merrymercy @hnyls2002 @cctry

Could one of you add `run-ci` and take the review? If the executor approach is not the direction you want, I would genuinely rather hear that than keep the branch alive — but #30770 is a real bug on current `main` with a second party patching around it, so I do not think the right outcome is for it to keep aging.

@chromecast56 @JianWang97 Thanks for building on #30771 in #39716 and #44502 and preserving the attribution. I want to consolidate this work into one merge path; I am happy for either #30771 or #39716 to carry it, with the original implementation/tests and subsequent contributions credited.

I updated #30771 to main and removed the OpenAI conversion hunk already covered by #39771. I also revisited the shared-tokenizer review on #39716. With the actual regular-tokenization method and pinned `tokenizers==0.23.2`, a synthetic CPU WordLevel probe still makes loop-side padding wait behind the shared backend (~246–257 ms, versus ~0.1 ms with a separate backend). This is not a model-serving benchmark, and the current head does not yet address that ownership issue.

I am preparing a narrower revision that passes a worker-owned fast-tokenizer backend explicitly to regular tokenization, leaving unsupported tokenizer types on their existing synchronous path. This follows the isolation direction already developed in #39716 without taking over its broader endpoint/ordering work.

Would you prefer to fold the focused fix/tests into #39716, or use #30771 as its small prerequisite and fold #44502 back here? Jian, validation of the final candidate on your workload would be especially helpful. I will keep this PR open until we agree on the target and attribution, rather than closing or replacing anyone's work prematurely.

## Code Review

This pull request improves event loop responsiveness by offloading potentially blocking operations, such as request conversion and tokenization, to separate threads using `asyncio.to_thread`. It also introduces unit tests to verify that these operations do not block the event loop. The review feedback highlights a critical thread-safety concern: slow tokenizers implemented in pure Python are not thread-safe and running them concurrently in separate threads can lead to race conditions or crashes. It is recommended to serialize access to slow tokenizers using a lock.

Impact:

- That can delay lightweight liveness endpoints such as `/ping` and `/health` even while the backend is otherwise alive.

Hi @merrymercy @hnyls2002 — gentle ping on this one. Routing to you two as the most active recent committers on `tokenizer_manager.py` / `http_server.py` (apologies if someone else is a better fit).

Quick summary for triage:
- **Problem**: synchronous request preprocessing blocks the TokenizerManager event loop, so `/health` stalls while tokens are still generating → Kubernetes liveness kills otherwise-healthy pods. We hit this in production at Toss Securities (271 gateway 502s from liveness restarts under load).
- **Fix**: offload the blocking preprocessing to a single-thread executor — no behavior change otherwise.
- **Status**: branch is up to date with `main` (0 behind), 142 tests pass locally (137 existing + 5 new, including an ASGI reproducer). The remaining red checks are the `pr-test-*-finish` gates — the underlying test stages show as skipped, so I believe CI just needs a maintainer trigger.

We are seeing the same false-health-check issue in production with DeepSeek-V4-Flash on SGLang v0.5.16: synchronous request preprocessing can starve `/health` while inference is still making progress.

We backported this PR onto our existing v0.5.16 image and ran the same 448-concurrent-client load test with ~64k-token chat inputs. Before the patch, the baseline produced 4 new readiness timeouts in the first minute. With this PR applied, the same load ran for 10+ minutes with zero readiness timeouts, zero liveness timeouts, and zero request errors.

Rebased onto current `main` and re-verified end to end. Putting the case for merging in one place, because I think this one has sat long enough.

## The bug still reproduces on today's `main`

I re-ran the reproducer from #30770 against current `main` with only the new tests applied and no production change: both starvation tests **fail**. With this PR applied they pass. So this is not a historical report — the synchronous preprocessing path is still on the event loop today, two months after the issue was filed.

Concretely, `OpenAIServingBase.handle_request()` calls `_convert_to_internal_request()` synchronously (Jinja render + `tokenizer.encode()`), and `TokenizerManager._tokenize_texts()` has a synchronous fallback. Both run on the same uvicorn loop as `/ping`, `/health` and `/health_generate`.

## Why the failure mode is worse than "a slow endpoint"

The engine is fine the whole time. Inference keeps making progress; only the loop cannot get a turn to answer the probe. So an orchestrator with a liveness probe restarts a **healthy** server, drops its in-flight requests, and pushes that load onto the remaining replicas — which then starve the same way. A transient burst becomes a rolling restart, and nothing in the logs points at preprocessing. That is why #30770 uses `/ping` rather than `/health`: it isolates loop responsiveness from generation health.

## Independent production confirmation

@yongqinwang-cmd hit this on a different model and a different deployment, backported the patch, and measured it (see above): 4 readiness timeouts in the first minute before, zero over 10+ minutes after, at 448 concurrent clients with ~64k-token inputs. They are carrying it as a local patch today.

## The change is small and deliberately conservative

`+412/-11` across 5 files, of which **378 lines are tests**. The production change is 29 added lines:

- A `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)` — *single* worker on purpose. Preprocessing is moved off the loop but stays serialized, so this cannot trade event-loop starvation for CPU oversubscription under a container quota.
- `copy_context().run(...)` so contextvars survive the thread hop.
- Both blocking paths routed through it.

## What I fixed in this push

Two things had rotted while the branch waited, both now handled:

- `_tokenize_texts` began consulting `model_config.is_embedding_gemma` after these tests were written, so the bare-manager test needed that attribute stubbed.
- The registered-test taxonomy (`test/registered/<kind>/<subsystem>/`) landed since the branch was opened, and the ASGI liveness test was outside it. Moved to `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/`; `check_registered_tests.py` and `check_no_registered_tests_in_package.py` now both pass.

Verified locally: the two CPU responsiveness tests pass with the patch and fail without it. The ASGI test could not run in my environment (`mlx` is not installable here), so I am relying on CI for that one.

## What is actually blocking this

Per [MAINTAINER.md](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md), this PR never got past step 2 — no Merge Oncall was ever assigned — so step 3 never happened either and it has **no `run-ci` label**. Every red check above is `pr-gate` refusing to start; not one test has ever run on this branch in CI. I am not in `.github/CI_PERMISSIONS.json`, so `/tag-and-rerun-ci` is a no-op for me.

Step 4 permits pinging other area oncalls when the assigned one is unresponsive. This touches `srt/entrypoints` and `srt/managers`:

- Router / API — @slin1237
- Scheduler — @merrymercy @hnyls2002 @cctry

Could one of you add `run-ci` and take the review? If the executor approach is not the direction you want, I would genuinely rather hear that than keep the branch alive — but #30770 is a real bug on current `main` with a second party patching around it, so I do not think the right outcome is for it to keep aging.

## Code Review

This pull request improves event loop responsiveness by offloading potentially blocking operations, such as request conversion and tokenization, to separate threads using `asyncio.to_thread`. It also introduces unit tests to verify that these operations do not block the event loop. The review feedback highlights a critical thread-safety concern: slow tokenizers implemented in pure Python are not thread-safe and running them concurrently in separate threads can lead to race conditions or crashes. It is recommended to serialize access to slow tokenizers using a lock.
